subject: general
question: Which is the largest river by volume in the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amazon**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Amazon River is the largest river by discharge volume of water in the world.
 
• It has an average discharge of about 209,000 cubic meters per second (7,381,000 cubic feet per second).
 
• The Amazon River is approximately 4,345 miles (7,062 kilometers) long, making it one of the longest rivers in the world.
 
• The river flows through several countries in South America, including Brazil, Peru, and Colombia, and its basin is home to the Amazon Rainforest, the largest rainforest in the world.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nile River**

 
 
• The Nile is commonly known as the longest river in the world, stretching about 6,650 kilometers (4,130 miles).
 
• It flows through northeastern Africa, including countries like Egypt, Sudan, and Uganda.
 
• The Nile has two major tributaries: the White Nile and the Blue Nile.
 
• It is crucial for agriculture and livelihoods in the regions it passes through, especially in Egypt.
 
 
 
• **Indus River**
 
 
• The Indus River is one of the longest rivers in the world, flowing through China (Tibet), India, and Pakistan.
 
• It is approximately 3,180 kilometers (1,976 miles) long.
 
• The river is crucial for the economy of Pakistan, especially for agriculture.
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization, one of the world's oldest civilizations, developed around this river.
 
 
 
• **Hwang Ho (Yellow River)**
 
 
• The Yellow River, or Hwang Ho, is the second-longest river in China, after the Yangtze River.
 
• It is approximately 5,464 kilometers (3,395 miles) long.
 
• It is often referred to as the "cradle of Chinese civilization" as its basin was the birthplace of ancient Chinese civilizations.
 
• The river is known for its heavy silt load, which gives it a distinctive yellow color.
